paper_title: General progress substitutes for specific training data in language models

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Language models acquire their capabilities from training data, and developers withhold data during training to keep models from learning capabilities that could be misused. How long this delays a capability, and how much data is needed to acquire it later, is unknown. Here we show that the general progress a model makes on the rest of its training data substitutes for the data that was withheld. We withheld the training signal for individual skills in models of chess, Othello, molecular strings, bracket languages and web text. The delay of a withheld skill in larger models was predicted from smaller ones. A chess model never explicitly trained to respond to check ranked the legal responses almost as well as a model that was. When models were then trained on the withheld data, they acquired the skill with a small fraction of the data needed from initialization, and this fraction decreased as the models progressed. A control rule of equal difficulty was learned much more slowly. A programming language withheld from the training text of a 7-billion-parameter model was regained in the same way. Data filtering therefore delays a capability, and the data required to regain it decreases as models improve.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Developers shape the capabilities of language models through their training data. Mixtures are tuned to balance domains (Ye et al., 2025; Liu et al., 2025; Xie et al., 2023), and documents or individual targets are removed to withhold capability that could be misused (OBrien et al., 2026; Rathi and Radford, 2026; Maini et al., 2025). The effect of such filter depends on how long it holds the capability back as the model improves and on how much data the model needs to acquire the capability once the data return. Scaling laws relate compute, data and model size to loss (Kaplan et al., 2020; Hoffmann et al., 2022), and loss indexes when skills appear (Du et al., 2024; Xia et al., 2023). Neither gives how much of skill comes from its own examples and how much from the rest of the training data. Earlier results show that the rest of the corpus contributes to skill. Pretraining reduces the data later task needs (Hernandez et al., 2021; Tripuraneni et al., 2020), capabilities suppressed by pruning or unlearning are regained with little further training (Lo et al., 2024; Deeb and Roger, 2024), and progress accumulates before score moves (Barak et al., 2022; Nanda et al., 2023a). The closest study is that of Rathi and Radford (Rathi and Radford, 2026), who filtered medical domain from models of 61M to 1.8B parameters. They found that filtering becomes more effective with scale and that adversarial fine-tuning restores the unfiltered baseline with less than 0.2% of the pretraining tokens, share that falls with model size. These studies do not give the size of the delay, how the cost of acquiring withheld capability depends on the models progress, or control for whether the saving is specific to the withheld skill. Here we show that withholding capabilitys training data delays the capability by predictable amount, that progress on the rest of the corpus substitutes for the withheld data, and that acquiring the capability once its data return becomes cheaper as models improve. We use target thinning, which removes fixed fraction of 1 skills next-token targets from the training loss while every input token stays in the text, and then return the targets. Models are compared at matched background loss, the prediction error on held-out text outside the thinned targets. The experiments cover chess and Othello (Toshniwal et al., 2022; Li et al., 2023; Nanda et al., 2023b; Karvonen, 2024; McGrath et al., 2022), molecular SMILES strings (Weininger, 1988; Schwaller et al., 2019; Varadi et al., 2025), Dyck languages (Hewitt et al., 2020; Wen et al., 2023) and web text, in models of up to 7 billion parameters. For king safety in chess, and for the capitals of countries in 7-billion-parameter web-text model, the delay follows, with no fitted parameter, from model that keeps all of the skills targets and one that keeps none; for the other skills the same form holds with fitted parameters. model that never received the targets has learned much of the skill, and when the targets return it acquires the skill with small fraction of the data needed from initialization. This cost falls as the model progresses: for each logit by which supervised model at the same progress exceeds the acquisition level, about tenfold in chess and web text and fourfold in SMILES. These relations predict both trends reported by Rathi and Radford. The deficit that filter leaves widens with progress, and the same progress makes the capability cheaper to acquire once its data return.

sections.title: 2.1 Delay from thinning a skill’s targets
sections.content: We asked by how much skill is delayed when only fraction of its examples is supervised. We trained decoder-only transformers whose hyperparameters transfer across scales (Dey et al., 2025; Yang et al., 2021) and kept fraction 𝑓 of the next-token targets selected by skill-specific rule, the retained fraction, while every input token stayed in the sequence (Fig. 1a). In chess the rule is king safety, which applies when the side to move is in check, on about 7% of boards. King-safety competence 𝑞 is the probability that the model assigns to legal escapes from check, relative to legal plus king-unsafe moves. Background loss 𝐿 is the held-out prediction error on all positions outside the thinned targets. Comparing models at the same 𝐿 separates the effect of skills own targets from progress on the rest of the corpus (Fig. B1). We measured the delay as shift of onset, the background loss at which competence reaches fixed level. In 9.7M-parameter chess models, keeping 10% of in-check targets moved onset at competence of 0.70 by 0.40 nats towards lower background loss (Fig. 1e). Removing an equal density of random targets left onset unchanged, and giving every in-check target loss weight of 0.1 produced the same competence as keeping 10% at full weight (Fig. B2h,i). For king safety in chess, the delay can be derived from model that keeps all of the targets and one that keeps none. sections.title: 2.2 Outputs of a never-supervised model
sections.content: The derivation attributes part of skill to the rest of the corpus, so we examined what model trained without skills targets predicts at the skills positions. We assigned every output token at 8,313 held-out in-check positions to class of move (Fig. 2a). chess model trained without in-check targets placed about half of its probability on moves that would be legal if the king were not in check, 0.48 for the 64M model at its last snapshot against 0.02 for the fully supervised model. Where two or more replies were legal, its most probable legal reply was the move played in the game at 0.64 of positions, against 0.68 for the fully supervised model and 0.30 by chance (Fig. 2b). Under target thinning, replies to check remain in the text the model reads. We therefore trained chess models on games in which no check occurs. At the first check of held-out game, these models ranked the move played first among the legal replies in 0.650.68 of games at 9.7M163M parameters, against 0.680.71 for fully supervised models. sections.title: 2.3 Cost of acquiring a withheld skill
sections.content: We measured how much data never-supervised model needs to acquire the skill once its targets return. We returned the targets at checkpoints along the training of source model, model trained without the skills targets, and trained until competence reached fixed level, the acquisition level (Fig. 3a). The acquisition cost is the number of tokens this took, relative to the tokens same-size model needs to reach the level from initialization (Hernandez et al., 2021). When the targets returned, chess source models had king-safety competence of 0.320.50, below the acquisition level. From each source runs lowest-loss checkpoint, acquisition required at most 0.100.78% of the tokens needed from initialization, and 3.17.5% when the 50 preceding steps that restore the optimizer state, which contain none of the returned targets, are also counted (Fig. D1e). To test whether this saving is specific to the withheld skill, we used control rule that applies one fixed permutation of the move labels to every in-check target. The permuted rule matches the true escapes in entropy and attainable accuracy, but its targets are the permuted labels and not the escaping moves, and from initialization the two rules needed the same number of tokens to within factor of 1.06. From the same source checkpoints, the permuted rule needed 2.416 times the tokens of the true rule (Fig. 3b). The cost changed little with batch size. For returns of 25 steps or more, fourfold smaller batch needed 1.11.65 times the tokens in 4.36.6 times as many steps (Fig. D1j). We asked what determines the cost across checkpoints, model sizes and returned shares. For returned share 𝑠, the acquisition loss is the background loss at which model trained with that share from the start reaches the acquisition level. The logit distance is the log odds of the acquisition level minus the log odds of same-size model trained with the returned share, read at the background loss at which the targets return. negative distance, which we call surplus, means that the source model has passed the acquisition loss. Source models that received their targets before reaching the acquisition loss acquired the skill when their own background loss reached it, with median difference of at most 0.04 nats, and their cost was the training needed to get there (Fig. 4b and Fig. D2h). Below the acquisition loss, each logit of surplus lowered the cost about tenfold in chess and web text and fourfold in SMILES. The cost fell by 1.12 0.04 decades per logit in chess, 0.91 0.04 in web text and 0.59 0.07 in SMILES, in 312 runs from 27 source runs (Fig. 4a,c and Fig. D2). The rates differed between the domains. At its acquisition loss model needed 30%, 24% and 38% of the tokens from initialization in chess, web text and SMILES. In Othello, never-supervised models acquired the forced-pass rule within about eight optimizer steps at every distance up to 0.85 logits above the acquisition loss (Fig. D2f). Logit distance predicted the cost better than the models score. Among 207 runs from source models scoring near their floor, logit distance ordered 85% of the pairs within domain by their cost, whereas the score when the targets returned ordered 53% (Fig. 4d). To test whether the effect of return is specific to its checkpoint, we added the part of its weight change that is due to the returned targets, without training, to other checkpoints of the same chess source run. sections.title: 2.4 Returns at 7 billion parameters
sections.content: To test the cost relation at larger scale, we withheld the targets that state countrys capital in 7-billionparameter web-text models, kept every input, and returned the targets at six checkpoints in each of two seeds. From the last three checkpoints, in order, one seed reached the acquisition level with 15%, 11% and 1.8% of the tokens needed from initialization and the other with 22%, 12% and 1.1%. From the three earlier checkpoints neither seed reached it (Fig. 3c and Fig. E1a,c). permuted assignment of capitals to countries needed 12 times the tokens of the true one from the final checkpoint, and 1.3 times from initialization. 8 At the same logit distance, the 7B costs were close to those of much smaller models (Fig. 4a), at 0.281.45 times the values of the single line fitted to chess, web text and SMILES at 9.7M431M (Fig. 4b,e). Across those sizes, the cost at given logit distance fell by further 0.28 0.09 decades for each tenfold increase in size (Fig. 4e). whole domain returned in the same way. 7B model trained with Rust documents filtered to 3% of their share predicted Rust terms with 52% accuracy, against 76% for the unfiltered model at matched background loss. Continued on the unfiltered corpus, it closed half of this gap with 2.1% of the tokens the unfiltered model had needed from initialization to reach the same accuracy (Fig. 3f and Fig. E1j). On 212 Rust function tasks it compiled 18% of its sampled completions at the return, against 45% for the unfiltered model, and 37% against 41% after 13% of its training tokens (Fig. 3f). Of 12 models of 20M300M parameters trained without astronomy, Rust or Chinese documents, 11 closed half of the accuracy gap with 1.97.5% of the domain tokens needed from initialization, and this share showed no trend with model size (Fig. 3d,e and Fig. E2g).

sections.title: 2.5 Removal route and earlier supervision
sections.content: We compared never-supervised source models with models from which learned skill had been removed. In chess models from 9.7M to 163M parameters and at matched background loss, these were models whose targets were withdrawn after the skill was learned and models from which the skill was unlearned by gradient ascent (Jang et al., 2023) or by misdirecting its representation (Li et al., 2024). With all targets returned, never-supervised models needed 520 times more tokens, depending on the route, than models that had once had the skill and started from the same legal-move probability mass (Fig. 5a,b and Fig. F1a,c). With 10% of the targets returned, never-supervised models reached the acquisition level in 5 of 13 cases, and models from the other routes in 51 of 52, of which 26 were at that level when the targets returned (Fig. 5c and Fig. F1b). When training resumed without in-check targets, models unlearned by gradient ascent rose to king-safety competence of 0.810.91 within 12 steps, whereas never-supervised models moved by less than 0.03 (Fig. 5d). The size of this advantage depended on how far the removal had lowered the skill. In SMILES models with ring closure removed, never-supervised models needed 411 times the tokens of models that had once had the skill. In 300M web-text models, neither withdrawal nor gradient ascent brought subjectverb agreement down to the never-supervised level, and never-supervised models needed 0.82.7 times the tokens of the others (Fig. F1ik). These comparisons agree with reports of faster relearning after unlearning (Rathi and Radford, 2026; Lee et al., 2025) and of recovery under training on unrelated data (Hu et al., 2025; Łucki et al., 2025; Siddiqui et al., 2025). Partial supervision before the return also lowered the cost. At matched background loss, 9.7M chess models that had kept 3% of in-check targets needed one-quarter as much training after the targets returned as models that had kept none (ratio 0.25, 95% interval 0.210.31; Fig. 5e). Related content accounted for part of the corpus support. Removing supervision on related king-safety positions, boards outside check where move that obeys the piece-movement rules would expose the king, reduced the fitted corpus support by 63%, whereas random removals reduced it by 33% or 19%, close to the shares of positions removed (Fig. 5f). We asked how much of the network must change to acquire the skill. With single upper block or adapters (Hu et al., 2021) of rank 4 or 16 trainable, the return needed 1.37.4 times the tokens of return that trains every parameter, which keeps 5996% of the saving, counted in decades (Fig. 5h). Removing the representation through which attacked squares drive king moves raised the cost by 2.9% (Fig. 5g). Source models assembled from the lower blocks of one checkpoint and the upper blocks of another of the same run had acquisition costs between those of the two checkpoints (Fig. 5i). sections.title: 3 Discussion
sections.content: In five domains and models of up to 7 billion parameters, thinning skills training targets delayed the skill by an amount that small models predicted for larger ones. For king safety in chess and for capital recall at 7 billion parameters, the delay follows with no fitted parameter from fully supervised and never-supervised model at the same background loss; the other skills required fitted sensitivity. Models trained without the targets had learned part of the skill from the rest of the corpus. When the targets returned, they acquired the skill with small fraction of the data needed from initialization, and each logit of surplus lowered this cost about tenfold in chess and web text and fourfold in SMILES. Both trends reported by Rathi and Radford (Rathi and Radford, 2026) follow from these relations. Corpus support falls as model progresses, so equation (2) gives deficit that widens with progress, and larger models progress further. By the cost relation, the same progress lowers the data needed to acquire the capability once its data return. Our measurements add the size of the delay, comparisons at matched background loss and permuted rule that tests whether the saving is specific to the withheld skill. Filtered models of 6.9 billion parameters resisted adversarial fine-tuning on 300M tokens (OBrien et al., 2026), 0.055% of their pretraining tokens. In our 7B model, the filtered domain returned with up to 13% of the models training tokens. For data filtering, the results separate the delay at given background loss from the cost of acquiring the skill once its data are available. Chess models trained on games without check ranked legal replies nearly as fully supervised models did, so filter that removed every example of the skill left much of it to be learned from the remaining games. The cost of acquiring the skill once its data returned fell as the model progressed, and it depended on how the skill had been removed. Never-supervised chess models needed 520 times more tokens than models from which learned skill had been removed. Document filtering and removing targets from the loss (OBrien et al., 2026; Rathi and Radford, 2026) therefore affect both models competence and the cost of adding the skill afterwards. For evaluation, the score on withheld skill was weaker guide to this cost than logit distance. Longer pretraining can lower the quality model reaches after fixed fine-tune (Springer et al., 2025), and extended training on sequence of tasks can reduce networks ability to learn (Dohare et al., 2024). On withheld skill, by contrast, the data needed to reach fixed competence fell with general progress. The change that completed skill was small relative to the network. With single upper block or adapters of rank 4 or 16 trainable, king safety was acquired with 1.37.4 times the tokens of return that trains every parameter, and the weight change of return raised legal-move mass at later checkpoints of the same run. This agrees with reports that pretraining lowers the number of parameters that adaptation requires (Aghajanyan et al., 2021) and that setting fewer than 0.05% of pretrained models weights to zero can match full fine-tuning (Lu et al., 2026).

sections.title: 4.1 Domains and data
sections.content: Training corpora are contiguous token streams read once in order, so the batch schedule fixes the data order. Chess: rated Lichess games from 2024 between players rated at least 1,500, one move per token. Othello: uniformly sampled legal games (Li et al., 2023) with an explicit pass token. SMILES: 300M canonical molecular strings from ZINC22 (Tingle et al., 2023), modelled at the character level. Dyck-4: well-formed nested sequences over four bracket pairs. Web text: FineWeb-Edu (Penedo et al., 2024) for models of up to 163M parameters and the Dolma 1.7 recipe of DataDecide (Magnusson et al., 2025) for models of 20M7B.

sections.title: 4.2 Models and training
sections.content: All models are dense pre-norm decoder-only transformers, with width and depth scaled together across seven sizes from 0.76M to 163M non-embedding parameters, and chess models of 431M, 1.28B and 3.0B. CompleteP parameterization (Dey et al., 2025) (𝛼 = 1), anchored at 2.2M parameters, transfers learning rates across sizes. The main recipe uses AdamW (Loshchilov and Hutter, 2019) with peak learning rate of 0.004, weight decay 0.1 and warm-upstabledecay schedule indexed in tokens per parameter. The constant-rate chess models (9.7M3.0B) use 15M-token warm-up and batches of 64 sequences. Sequences have 2,048 tokens. FineWeb-Edu models use constant learning rate of 0.008 after warm-up. Dolma models have the Llama architecture as implemented in HuggingFace Transformers, without CompleteP, and use weight decay 0.05, batches of 128 sequences and, after 32-step warm-up, constant learning rate of 2.12 103 at 20M300M, 1.06 103 at 1B and 2.65 104 at 7B; the 300M and 1B models with the designs of the two 7B models (models and below) use the 7B rate. Seeds change the weight initialization and read the same data stream; in the Dolma models seed also sets the data order.

sections.title: 4.3 Competence, background loss and target thinning
sections.content: Target thinning removes the next-token loss at skills targets unless ℎ( 𝑝) < 𝑓 , with ℎ deterministic hash of the stream position 𝑝 and 𝑓 the retained fraction. Inputs are never changed, and the training loss is the mean cross-entropy over the retained targets. The thinned targets are in-check boards in chess (7.1% of tokens), forced passes in Othello (0.73%) and ring-closing digits in SMILES (5.17%). In web text, programmatic labellers mark closing brackets, number-marked auxiliaries, repeated 4-gram completions and counting sequences, and two factual relations, country capitals and city countries, are thinned by masking answer mentions within 128 tokens after their subject. Competence is read on fixed held-out split. In chess, every vocabulary token at an in-check board is assigned to an exact legality class, and king-safety competence is 𝑞 = legal/(legal + king-unsafe) probability mass. Competence is the probability of the pass token at forced-pass positions in Othello, of the true closing digit in SMILES and, for web-text agreement, of the true form relative to the true plus the other-number form of is/are, was/were and has/have. Background loss is the held-out cross-entropy, in nats, at all targets outside the thinned ones; in Othello it is taken at positions with two or more legal squares, and in the Dolma models at targets outside every labelled class. Onset is the background loss, interpolated between log-spaced checkpoints (2136 per chess run on the warm-upstabledecay schedule and 5276 on the constant rate), at which competence crosses stated level: 𝑞 = 0.70, 0.75 and 0.80 in chess, where 𝑞 = 0.659 lies on the plateau of the fully supervised trajectories, 0.4 in Othello and 0.6 in SMILES. Runs that do not reach level are censored at their final background loss. Probes are class-balanced logistic regressions on residual-stream activations, scored against an identically probed random network, and causal use is the effect of ablating variables difference-of-means direction relative to random directions (Geiger et al., 2024) (Fig. B1i).

sections.title: 4.4 Derived thinning relation
sections.content: Equations (1) and (2) are the form weighted likelihood takes when the skills targets enter with weight 𝑓 and the rest of the corpus with weight 𝜏. For each of 4,173 held-out in-check positions, the probability mass on legal and on king-unsafe moves at every snapshot of the fully supervised and the never-supervised model was interpolated, in log, to 0.05-nat grid of background loss. The derived offset at retained fraction 𝑓 adds ln[( 𝑓 + 𝜏)/(1 + 𝜏)] to the log odds of every position of the fully supervised model and pools the masses as for 𝑞; 𝜏 at each background loss is the value at which 𝑓 = 0 reproduces the pooled odds of the never-supervised model. Root-mean-square differences from the measured offsets, over models and background losses, are 0.039 logits (95% interval 0.0310.047) for 15 thinned 9.7M models of two seeds at nine retained fractions, and 0.089 logits (0.0420.119) for 64M models at 𝑓 = 0.3, 0.1, 0.03 and 0.01 (Fig. 1c). With each positions own never-supervised odds in equation (1), in place of the common 𝜏, the differences are 0.20 and 0.32 logits. 12 Because 𝑞 pools the mass of all positions, small uniform shift of the log odds changes the pooled log odds, to first order, by the shift times 1 Var(𝑞𝑥)/[𝑞(1 𝑞)], where 𝑞𝑥 is the competence of the fully supervised model at position 𝑥 and 𝑞 its mass-weighted mean; this factor is 0.590.66 at 1.852.75 nats. The pooled form, logit 𝑞(𝐿, 𝑓 ) logit 𝑞(𝐿, 1) = 𝜅 ln[( 𝑓 + 𝜏)/(1 + 𝜏)], is fitted with sensitivity 𝜅 and corpus support 𝜏 at each background loss, to positive fractions only, over all thinned chess models (Fig. B2k). At 64M, 𝜏 is 0.96, 0.85 and 0.80 times the 9.7M value at 1.85, 1.95 and 2.05 nats. The same test on thinned 9.7M models of six further skills ( 𝑓 = 0.010.5; one to three seeds per skill) gives root-mean-square errors of 0.80 logits for SMILES ring closure, 0.32 for SMILES branch closing, 0.71 for the Othello forced pass, 0.32 for the Othello forced move, 1.71 for Dyck closing brackets at match distances of 27 and 0.26 for web-text subjectverb agreement, against 0.31, 0.20, 0.42, 0.19, 0.39 and 0.10 for the pooled form fitted at each background loss. The derived offset is too shallow by 0.240.50 logits in the three skills whose never-supervised model has no competence and too deep by 0.220.23 in two whose never-supervised model has some; for the Dyck skill, whose never-supervised model reaches competence of 0.270.43, it is too shallow by 1.36. In every skill, 𝜏 falls as background loss falls. At 7B, three models at each of seeds 0 and 1, with one data order per seed, keep all, none and fraction 0.3 of the capital targets: the never-supervised models follow the recipe, seed and data order of the source models of the capital returns, the fully supervised models their references, and the thinned models follow the same recipe. At each stored snapshot we scored 816 capital prompts by the probability of the correct answer among the 102 answers and interpolated the log odds of each prompt linearly in background loss to 16 losses from 3.05 to 3.80 nats, range spanned by seven or eight snapshots of each model. The derived offset shifts the log odds of every prompt of the fully supervised model by ln[( 𝑓 + 𝜏)/(1 + 𝜏)], with 𝜏 the value at which 𝑓 = 0 reproduces the pooled competence of the never-supervised model of the same seed, and pools. Over the 32 offsets it differs from the measured offset by 0.14 logits (root mean square; 0.13 in seed 0 and 0.14 in seed 1), deeper by 0.10 logits on average in seed 0 and shallower by 0.09 in seed 1. The retained fraction alone (𝜏 = 0) misses by 0.61 logits (0.69 and 0.52) and the offset of the never-supervised model by 0.43; with the never-supervised model of the other seed the error is 0.17 logits. Over the four lowest losses the error is 0.12 logits in seed 0 and 0.25 in seed 1, where the measured offset is deeper than the derived one and within 0.12 logits of the retained fraction alone. The measured offsets of the two seeds differ by 0.31 logits (0.44 over the four lowest losses). On country recall, whose targets all six models keep, the thinned and the fully supervised model differ by 0.09 logits. The test covers one retained fraction (Fig. B2n). For 18 skills of the four domains thinned to 𝑓 = 0.5, 0.3, 0.1 and 0.03 at 9.7M, the horizontal shift that aligns each thinned curve with its fully supervised curve is fitted as 𝐴𝑘 (1 𝑓 𝑝) (Fig. B2cg).

sections.title: 4.5 Held-out predictions
sections.content: Each chess test fits the pooled form to calibration runs only and predicts the thinned trajectories of held-out model from its seed-mean fully supervised trajectory, with no parameter refitted. The four tests hold out fractions below 0.1, model sizes, the constant-learning-rate schedule and the 1.28B and 3.0B models, for which the predicted fraction, 𝑓 = 0.1, is included at every calibration size. The error is the root-mean-square logit offset error of trajectory (Fig. B2a,b). On web text, two sets of 24 runs vary the fractions of the four labelled classes, and of capitals and city countries, in Latin-square designs ( 𝑓 = 1, 0.3, 0.1; two seeds), with five and two further runs at 1B. The response is calibrated at competence levels 0.30.7 with censored fits of the onset against ln 𝑓 and log10 parameters, and only the shift in ln 𝑓 enters prediction. At 7B, model thins closing and counting to 0.3, agreement to 0.05 and capitals to 0.1, and model thins city countries to 0.1. Each skill is compared with the model in which it is fully supervised, whose trajectory the prediction shifts, and the error is the mean absolute difference between predicted and observed onset shift over six skills and three seeds (Fig. 1h and Fig. B5ac). In the isolated 13 contrasts, only long-range closing is thinned, to 0.3, or only agreement, to 0.05, at 150M and 300M with four seeds (Fig. B5di).

sections.title: 4.6 Document filtering
sections.content: A chess game filter with recall 𝛾 discards each game that contains check with probability 𝛾 and replaces it from the stream, which leaves density of in-check targets of 𝑓 (𝛾) = (1 𝛾)/[0.058 + 0.942(1 𝛾)]. On the constant-rate recipe, 9.7M64M models (two seeds) were trained with game filtering or target thinning at matched residual shares (0.1, 0.03 and 0) and compared on background loss over game prefixes before the first check, with delays read at legal-move mass of 0.6 (Fig. 1f and Fig. B4g,h). In web text, reference labels for astronomy (lexicon density), Rust (Rust-exclusive syntax) and Chinese (CJK share) mark 0.53%, 0.22% and 0.15% of the stream. hashed 𝑛-gram linear classifier over each documents first 512 tokens removes documents at thresholds that leave share 𝑓 of reference-labelled tokens. Below the lowest share that threshold alone reaches (0.1 for astronomy, 0.03 for Rust and 0.01 for Chinese), every reference-labelled document is also removed except hashed fraction 𝑓 of them. Models of 20M300M parameters were trained to 1.03.0B tokens in 6 6 Latin square that filters all three domains in every run, with two seeds (48 runs), together with 1B pair at 𝑓 = 1 and 0.03 and 7B pair for Rust, model with and without the filter at 𝑓 = 0.03. Competence is top-1 accuracy at tokens that require the domain skill in held-out domain documents (Fig. E2).

sections.title: 4.7 Chess games without a check
sections.content: The models trained on games without check are the game-filter models at recall 1 (seed 1; 600M tokens at 9.7M64M parameters and 450M at 163M); replay of their training stream with python-chess finds no in-check position. They are evaluated at the first check with played reply in each of 2,000 held-out games (1,704 positions, 1,533 with two or more legal replies), with the prompt ending at the checking move, against the model trained without in-check targets and the fully supervised model of the same size and seed at the saved checkpoint nearest in held-out loss before the first check. board pair consists of two of these positions in which the same piece on the same square has the same two non-capturing, non-checking moves, one resolving the check on the first board and leaving the king attacked on the second, and the other the reverse (18,701 pairs from 1,162 games; intervals resample games). With each game in at most one pair, the four models preferred the legal move on both boards in 0.570.72 of pairs (Table C1). For the transfer between replies, the 9.7M model was continued on 3,072 game prefixes that end at first check, with the loss on the reply played only. Each set of replies has one run, evaluated on 326 held-out knight checks and 92 held-out positions where every legal reply is block (Fig. C1).

sections.title: 4.8 Output classes at the skill’s positions
sections.content: For 8,313 in-check positions of 2,000 held-out chess games, each of the 1,970 output tokens was assigned with python-chess to one class: legal king moves, captures of the checking piece and interpositions; moves that would be legal if the king were not in check; king moves to an attacked square; moves that expose the king to further piece; and tokens that are not moves of the position. In the returns of Fig. 2c the model state was saved at the end of the warm-up before the return (step 0) and after steps 18, 10, 12 and 16 with the returned targets (2.1M tokens); over these states the share of positions whose most probable legal reply is the move played, taken as everywhere over the 7,149 positions with two or more legal replies, stayed at 0.580.59 for the return from 1.95 nats and at 0.620.64 for the return from 1.62 nats. The 23,190 SMILES ring-closure positions of Fig. 2d come from 8,000 held-out molecules.

sections.title: 4.9 Acquisition cost after targets return
sections.content: Chess. Returns start from source models trained without in-check targets (three seeds each at 9.7M, 24M, 64M and 431M) at background losses of 1.562.87 nats and train on unseen stream segments. The targets return at share 𝑠 = 1, 0.3, 0.1 or 0.03 with 131,072 tokens per step, in one of two return conditions. With the warm-up before the return, the AdamW second moments are estimated over 20 steps without parameter updates, the learning rate is warmed up over 30 steps without in-check targets, and the targets then return at full learning rate (110 runs). Costs count the tokens after the targets return; with these 50 steps also counted, the costs from each source runs lowest-loss checkpoint are 3.17.5%. With the warm-up at the return, 20-step warm-up starts when the targets return (188 runs; Fig. D1ad). Six returns of all targets from 9.7M and 64M checkpoints at 2.993.99 nats use the warm-up before the return. Competence and background loss are evaluated on 1,000 held-out games when the targets return and then at steps spaced by factor of 1.25. The cost is the number of tokens from the return to the first evaluation at or above the acquisition level, interpolated from the evaluation before it, divided by the tokens same-size model needs from initialization. Acquisition is read on the in-check legal-move probability mass at level of 0.6, and king-safety competence 𝑞 is used for the thinning results; at the first crossing of 𝑞 = 0.659 in return, the legal-move mass has median of 0.60. Web text. Eleven source models of 9.7M163M parameters were trained on FineWeb-Edu for 464 tokens per parameter (64, 24 and 12 at 9.7M, 24M and 64M; 8 and 4 at 163M) without the targets of number-marked finite verbs. At return the AdamW moments are estimated as in chess, 30 steps on the source models own targets follow, and all agreement targets then return at 64 sequences per step on unseen rows (90 runs). Competence is evaluated at auxiliaries with noun subject in 384 held-out sequences and the acquisition level is 0.85. The denominator is the mean over runs from initialization at the same size, recipe and batch. SMILES. Ring-closing targets return to the 9.7M, 24M, 64M and 163M source models, one seed each, at seven to nine checkpoints per size with background losses of 0.480.85 nats (21, 19, 18 and 15 runs), at share of 1, 0.3, 0.1 or 0.03 (64M: 1, 0.3 or 0.1; 163M: 1 or 0.3) and 16 sequences per step, after 20 moment-estimation steps and with the warm-up at the return. Competence is evaluated on 8,000 held-out molecules, the acquisition level is 0.6, and budgets are 20M100M tokens by share. The denominator is the run from initialization of the same size and seed with the same batch and warm-up (11.3M, 11.6M, 15.8M and 20.7M tokens). Othello. All forced-pass targets return to eight source runs trained with none, 10% or 30% of them (53 runs), with the warm-up at the return and 64 sequences per step. Competence is evaluated on 2,000 held-out games, the acquisition level is 0.4 and the budget is 40M tokens. The denominator is the mean over the fully supervised runs of the same size.

sections.title: 4.10 Logit distance and the cost relation
sections.content: For each return, the acquisition loss 𝐿 (𝑠) is the background loss at which the reference for the returned share 𝑠 reaches the acquisition level. For the progress term and the split of the cost relation at 𝐿(𝑠), it is read from one curve per domain, fitted to the references across sizes and returned shares in chess, across returned shares at 9.7M in SMILES and across sizes in web text, which lies within 0.04 nats of the same-size reference in chess and SMILES and within 0.08 nats in web text. The reference is the model of the same size and recipe trained from initialization with fraction 𝑠 of the skills targets, of the same seed as the source run where its trajectory extends to 𝐿0 and of another seed otherwise. The logit distance is 𝑥 = ℓ ℓ𝑠 (𝐿0), with ℓ the log odds of the acquisition level and ℓ𝑠 (𝐿) the reference log odds, centred running mean over three checkpoints (five at 7B). 𝐿0 is the background loss at the first evaluation of the return run, when the targets return: after the 30 preceding steps in chess with the warm-up before the return and in web text, and at the stored checkpoint with the warm-up at the return (chess, SMILES and Othello). Acquisition cost is modelled as 𝑃 + 10 𝑎+𝑏 min(𝑥,0) . The progress term 𝑃 is the number of tokens the source run needs to bring its own background loss from 𝐿0 to 𝐿 (𝑠), divided by the tokens from initialization; it is zero when 𝐿0 𝐿 (𝑠) and has no parameter fitted to the costs. The main-text rates are from maximum-likelihood 15 fit with an intercept 𝑎, rate 𝑏 and residual variance for each domain and random intercept for each source run, over the 312 runs with reference that reached the acquisition level in chess (159 runs, 12 source runs), web text (88, 11) and SMILES (65, 4) at 9.7M431M parameters. The rates differ between domains (likelihood ratio 𝜒2 = 44.4, 2 degrees of freedom). The single line of Fig. 4b is the least-squares fit of one intercept and one rate to the same runs, 𝑎 = 0.53 and 𝑏 = 0.97 0.07, with residual standard deviation of 0.36 dex. The least-squares slope of its residuals against log10 parameters is the trend with model size (Fig. 4e). The 7B costs are not in the fit: the measured costs are 0.451.02 times the lines values in seed 0 and 0.281.45 times in seed 1, and the six censored returns have lower bounds 0.210.43 dex below 𝑃 + 10𝑎. Othello is not fitted: in 46 of its 53 runs the level was reached within five optimizer steps, the resolution of the cost measure. source model is near the floor when its score lies in the lowest 10% of the range between the median score of never-supervised models, taken above the acquisition loss, and the acquisition level; in chess this score is 𝑞, with the level of 0.659. Near-floor ordering is the share of pairs of runs within domain whose order of cost is identified and agrees with the order of the predictor: 0.85 for logit distance, 0.77 for background loss and 0.53 for the score when the targets return (Fig. 4d).

sections.title: 4.11 Batch size and learning rate at the return
sections.content: Chess source models at 9.7M, 24M and 64M parameters received all in-check targets, with the warm-up before the return, from three checkpoints each, with batches of 16, 64 or 256 sequences at the standard learning rate and of 64 or 16 sequences at one third of it. The warm-up used the setting of the return, every setting read the same token stream in two data orders, and each cost is divided by run from initialization at the same setting. Because the warm-up moves the background loss by an amount that depends on the setting, the logit distance is read here at the stored checkpoint. The slope of log10 relative cost against logit distance, pooled over sizes, was 1.03 0.07 decades per logit at the standard setting (18 runs) and 0.861.29 at the other four. From the lowest-loss checkpoint at 9.7M, the permuted rule needed 11.012.7 times the tokens of the true rule at the same settings (Fig. D1ik).

sections.title: 4.12 Transplanted weight changes
sections.content: In the two 9.7M chess source runs, the targets were returned at the 619M, 290M, 193M and 97M-token checkpoints with the warm-up before the return, each return was stopped at the first evaluation at which in-check legal-move mass reached 0.6, and its weight change was saved. control run from each checkpoint took the same number of steps on the sources own targets, and the change due to the returned targets is the difference between the two weight changes. It was added, without training, to each of the 22 saved checkpoints of the same run and of the other seeds run. The 193M change gave legal-move mass of 0.59 at its own checkpoint, 0.610.62 at every later one with rise in background loss of 0.040.05 nats, and 0.54 and 0.45 at 145M and 97M tokens. Across the checkpoints with measured acquisition cost, the rank correlation between the recipients cost and the mass gained from the 290M change was 0.95 and 0.77 in the two seeds. The changes gave no gain at the other seeds checkpoints, and neither did Gaussian change with the norm of the returns whole weight change in every tensor. The weight change of permuted-rule return at 619M tokens, read out on the permuted rule, gave 0.61 at its own checkpoint and 0.41, 0.30, 0.16 and 0.11 at the four earlier ones. In two 64M source runs with 31 checkpoints each, the 226M change, 1.5% of the weight norm, gave 0.58 at the next checkpoint and 0.630.65 from 322M to 1.93B tokens with rise in background loss of 0.010.02 nats, and the permuted-rule change from 226M tokens gave 0.62 at its own checkpoint, 0.37 at the next and 0.07 at the last (Fig. F1lo).

sections.title: 4.13 Returned targets at 7B
sections.content: The 7B source model follows the recipe of models and with the targets of country capitals removed from the loss, together with agreement and repeated 4-gram targets, and every input kept, in seeds 0 and 16 1. Six snapshots between steps 2,048 and 12,817 are continued on the source models own data order. The capital targets return with the warm-up before the return, during which the source models masks apply. The acquisition level is capital competence of 0.20; the fully supervised references end at 0.33 and 0.39. The reference of each seed is fully supervised model with the recipe, data order and seed of its source model and the capital targets kept; it reaches the level after 1.67B tokens in seed 0 and 1.63B in seed 1, at background loss of 3.22 nats in both. Capital competence is smoothed over five evaluations in logit, and the level is reached at the first upward crossing of the smoothed curve. The returns from steps 12,817, 8,192 and 5,793 reached the level after 1.8%, 11.0% and 15.2% of the references tokens in seed 0 and after 1.1%, 12.3% and 22.3% in seed 1, and those from the three earlier steps did not reach it in either seed. The returns from step 12,817 start 0.013 and 0.017 nats below the lowest background loss of their reference, so their logit distance is read on model of seed 0. The permuted assignment maps the first answer token of each capital through one fixed derangement of the 102 answer groups, and matched true-rule control supervises the same positions with the true first token; both were run in seed 0 only. Agreement targets returned to the same six snapshots reached competence of 0.85 after 2.75.6% of the tokens needed by model of the same seed, which keeps the agreement targets (Fig. E1c,e). With only this token supervised, the permuted assignment needed 12.3, 3.9 and more than 1.4 times the tokens of the true assignment from steps 12,817, 8,192 and 4,096. 7B model of seed 0 that keeps every target of the recipe, with the capital targets permuted from initialization, reached the level after 1.29 times the tokens of the seed-0 reference.

sections.title: 4.14 Domains returned after filtering
sections.content: The Rust-filtered 7B model after 15,000 steps is continued with its optimizer state on the unfiltered corpus, at the same learning rate and batch, for 0.5B tokens on data blocks that neither it nor model has read, and model B, the unfiltered model of Fig. 3f, is continued from its own state on the same blocks. Term accuracy on the Rust evaluation documents is smoothed over five evaluations in logit, and the gap is the mean of model Bs first five evaluations minus the filtered models accuracy at the return (0.764 and 0.517). For each fraction of the gap, the tokens after the return are divided by the tokens at which model B, evaluated on the same documents from initialization, first reached that accuracy. Half of the gap closed after 9.4M tokens against 450M from initialization, three quarters after 3.4% and nine tenths after 13%. Before the return the filtered model had read 259,000 reference-labelled Rust tokens, the Rust content of 117M tokens of the unfiltered stream; with these counted, its Rust tokens at the three points are 28%, 13% and 18% of those model had read at the same accuracy. The data order of the 7B models reads rows that hold 55 of the 290 Rust evaluation documents. On the 235 that it does not read, the single-evaluation accuracies of model and the filtered model at the return are 0.746 and 0.509, against 0.753 and 0.517 on all documents, and the fraction of the gap closed at each of seven saved states of the continuation is within 0.02 of its value on all documents. Working behaviour is scored on 212 Rust function tasks: ten completions per task are sampled at temperature 0.8, compiled with the hidden assertions and run in sandbox, and compile and pass rates are fractions of the 2,120 completions. At the return the filtered model compiled 17.6% (95% interval 15.020.2) and model 44.7% (40.449.1); after 500M tokens the values were 37.4% (33.241.4) and 41.1% (37.045.3). At 20M300M, models trained with one domain removed ( 𝑓 = 0, seed 0) were continued on the unfiltered stream for 300 steps of 128 sequences, with new data order and 32-step learning-rate warm-up, and evaluated every 10 steps (Fig. E2g). Shares follow the 7B rule, in reference-labelled domain tokens. The log10 shares were fitted by maximum likelihood with censoring; the Chinese model at 300M is lower bound (5.9%). constant, 1.33 0.05 (4.7%) with residual standard deviation of 0.17 dex, was preferred to form with size term (+0.02 0.11 dex per tenfold increase) and gives 95% prediction interval of 1.911.9% at 7B (Fig. 3e).

sections.title: 4.15 Removal routes
sections.content: King safety is removed by four routes in 13 cases, each pairing fully supervised chess model with model of the same seed and training tokens trained without in-check targets, at 9.7M, 24M, 64M and 163M parameters and background losses of 1.651.96 nats, where the models of case agree within 0.015 nats. The two withdrawn routes continue the fully supervised model without in-check targets for 8M and for 64M tokens; when the targets return, the models withdrawn for 64M tokens are up to 0.12 nats below the never-supervised model of their case and the others within 0.04. Unlearning either trains by gradient ascent on the in-check loss (weight 0.3) with descent on the remaining loss (Jang et al., 2023), or pushes the residual stream at in-check positions towards fixed random direction while holding it to its value before unlearning elsewhere (Li et al., 2024); both keep the state of lowest competence whose background loss is at most 0.05 nats above the start. Every model then starts from fresh optimizer and receives the in-check targets with the warm-up before the return, at share of 1, 0.1 or 0. The matched comparison enters the never-supervised trajectory of the same case at the legal-move probability mass from which the other model starts and compares the tokens each then needs to reach mass of 0.6. On web text the routes are applied to subjectverb agreement in 300M models of the Dolma recipe, two seeds at two background losses each. Gradient ascent uses the two-way cross-entropy of the auxiliary against its number partner (weight 0.3, learning rate 104, 64 sequences per step); with ascent on the full cross-entropy, as in chess, competence stayed above 0.87 (Fig. F1ik). Withdrawal lowered competence to 0.650.74 and two-way ascent to 0.610.70, against 0.500.51 for never-supervised models, so the matched comparison of chess is made on competence (𝑛 = 7). Returns follow the chess procedure with 64 sequences per step, the acquisition level is 0.85, and costs are divided by the tokens at which the fully supervised run of the same seed reaches it. In SMILES the routes are applied to ring closure in 9.7M and 24M models, two seeds each, at 6 and 14 tokens per parameter (eight cases), with the chess settings and 16 sequences per step. Withdrawal lowered competence from 0.860.91 to 0.010.04, gradient ascent stopped at 0.160.47 and misdirection at 0.090.14, against at most 0.002 for never-supervised models.

sections.title: 4.16 Earlier supervision
sections.content: Two 9.7M chess models that kept 3% of in-check targets, and two trained on games filtered to residual share of 3%, received all in-check targets with the warm-up before the return. The reference is the set of such returns to models trained without in-check targets, whose log10 cost is fitted as cubic in background loss before the first check with an intercept for each size. The effect of earlier supervision is the mean, over the two models that kept 3%, of each models mean residual from the reference fit, and the ratio of 0.25 is ten to the power of this effect. Its 95% interval uses the variance between and within source runs of the reference, estimated with each source run left out in turn (Fig. 5e).

sections.title: 4.17 Related king-safety positions
sections.content: Family-masking runs in 9.7M chess models mask the targets on related king-safety boards, or on random families of 28.7% and 15.7% of positions, at in-check retained fractions 𝑓 = 0, 0.03, 0.3 and 1 with two paired seeds. For each seed, the models without masked family at the four fractions, 𝑓 = 0 included, give 𝜅(𝐿) and 𝜏(𝐿) at nine background losses from 1.90 to 2.10 nats. With these fixed, the offsets of the masked from the unmasked models are fitted by least squares with 𝐷𝑘 ( 𝑓 , 𝐿) = 𝑐𝑘 + 𝜅(𝐿) ln{[ 𝑓 + 𝜏(𝐿)(1 𝑟𝑘)]/[ 𝑓 + 𝜏(𝐿)]}, where 𝑐𝑘 does not depend on 𝑓 and 𝑟𝑘 is the fractional reduction in corpus support. The reported reduction is the mean of the two seed fits, and the range is over the 16 assignments of seed to each fraction (Fig. 5f).

sections.title: 4.18 Restricted returns, representation edit and stitched models
sections.content: Restricted returns start from the lowest-loss checkpoint of two chess source runs at each of 9.7M, 24M and 64M parameters and use the warm-up before the return with only selected parameters trainable: one transformer block, the final norm and unembedding, or rank-1, -4 or -16 low-rank adapters (Hu et al., 2021) on every block. Of three learning-rate multipliers (one, three and ten), the one with the cheapest permuted return was used for both rules. Costs are tokens to an in-check legal-move mass of 0.6 divided by those of the unrestricted return from the same checkpoint, and run that does not reach 0.6 within half the tokens from initialization is lower bound. The share of the saving kept is 1 log10(cost ratio)/log10 (tokens from initialization/tokens of the unrestricted return). Where both rules reached 0.6 under restriction, the permuted rule needed 1066 times more tokens. For the representation edit, distributed alignment search fitted rank-8 subspace at the token where the move is predicted, in the block with the highest held-out interchange transfer, at three checkpoints of each of eight chess source runs (9.7M and 24M parameters, four seeds each). The readout is king-move sensitivity, log 𝑝(𝐾 𝑠 𝑠 safe) log 𝑝(𝐾 𝑠 𝑠 attacked), on counterfactual position pairs from held-out games. The edit replaces the subspace by its mean at every token and removed 5064% of the readout. Each checkpoint was continued with the edit or with random rank-8 ablation, kept in place while the targets returned. The contrast is the paired difference in log10 tokens to legal-move mass of 0.6, averaged over source runs three checkpoints, with 90% 𝑡 interval over the eight source runs (Fig. 5g and Fig. F1fh). Stitched models take the embedding and the blocks below split 𝐾 from one checkpoint and the remaining blocks, final norm and unembedding from another checkpoint of the same chess source run, and receive the targets with the warm-up before the return in two data orders. Their costs are compared with the least-squares line of log cost against background loss at the return through the intact models of the same run (Fig. 5i).

sections.title: 4.19 Statistics
sections.content: The unit of replication is training run from one initialization seed. The thinned models of the controlled domains have three to five seeds per size up to 64M parameters and one to three at 163M and 431M; designs with one or two source runs per size are stated in their sections. Web text has two seeds per design at 300M and 1B, three at 7B and four per size in the isolated contrasts; the capital returns at 7B have two seeds, and the document-filter pair at 1B, the Rust-filtered 7B model and the domain returns at 20M300M are single runs at seed 0. The chess models trained on games without check have one seed per size, and each set of replies in the transfer test has one run. Checkpoints of run, and the returns that start from them, are repeated measurements of that run, so cost fits include random intercept for each source run or standard errors clustered by source run. value after is standard error, and intervals are 95% unless stated. Errors of the derived relation have intervals from resampling models. run that does not reach level within its budget is lower bound at the tokens it ran, and run at the level by its first evaluation is an upper bound. Bounds enter an ordering only where the order of the pair is identified, enter fits by maximum likelihood with censoring where stated, and are left out of least-squares fits of cost, as are runs without reference trajectory and the Othello runs.

sections.title: 4.20 Software
sections.content: Experiments and analyses used PyTorch 2.12, NumPy 2.5, SciPy 1.18, python-chess 1.11.2, RDKit (2021.03 for corpus generation and 2026.09 for evaluation), SELFIES 2.2.0, Numba 0.68, spaCy 3.8.7 and HuggingFace tokenizers 0.23 and Transformers 5.19. Figures were rendered in inklet 4.9; chess pieces use the vector set by Colin M. L. Burnett distributed with python-chess. Large language model assistants (Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini and OpenAI Codex) were used under the authors direction to assist with training and analysis code, checks of the labellers and manuscript editing; the authors verified every reported result and take full responsibility for the content.

sections.title: 4.21 Data availability
sections.content: All training corpora are public or generated from seed. Chess games are the rated games of JanuaryAugust 2024 in the Lichess database (https://database.lichess.org). SMILES strings are the first 300M molecules of the Hugging Face dataset chandar-lab/ZINC_22, without 830 that fail SELFIES round trip, and the held-out molecules are from the last 3M of the same split. Web text is from HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu and from the tokenized Dolma 1.7 files of allenai/DataDecide-data-recipes. Othello games and Dyck-4 sequences are generated from seed. The released code rebuilds the training streams, label arrays and held-out sets from these sources; its SMILES stream keeps the 830 molecules, so stream positions after the first of them differ from ours.

sections.title: 4.22 Code availability
sections.content: Code for building the corpora, training with target thinning, returning targets, the removal routes, document filtering and the fits of the thinning and cost relations is available at https://github.com/Mapika/ progress-substitutes-data under the MIT licence. Its README lists the analyses that the release leaves out, among them the Rust function tasks and the transplanted weight changes, and the points at which rerun differs from our runs.

sections.content: B.1 Domains and data Each controlled domain provides exact labels for its latent variables at every prefix, together with deterministic verifier. Othello and Dyck-4 have an exact Bayes-optimal predictor, which gives the floor of the cross-entropy. B.2 Models and training The seven base sizes have 0.755M, 2.21M, 4.82M, 9.67M, 24.4M, 64.4M and 162.8M non-embedding parameters. FineWeb-Edu models train with weight decay 0.1 and gradient clipping at 1. On the Dolma recipe the learning rate at 1B is half that of the 20M300M models, and the learning rate at 7B was selected by the lowest loss after 700 steps among three rates. Models and stop at 3.4B and 3.9B tokens. B.3 Competence, background loss and target thinning Masked positions are excluded from the numerator and the denominator of the training loss, so every other target keeps its loss term and its weight relative to the thinned targets changes. run that does not reach an onset level is censored at its final background loss, which is an upper bound on the background loss at which the level would be crossed. Background loss as the index (Fig. B1). For each skill, the logit competence of fully supervised runs is fitted as cubic in background loss (fifth degree for web text) on seed 0 of the smaller sizes, and the other seeds and the larger sizes are scored from that fit. Over the 98 runs left out of the fits, across 21 skills, the median absolute residual is 0.031 logits, and it is at most 0.16 logits for the 21 runs of 100M parameters or more. Loss weight against thinning (Fig. B2h). In 9.7M chess models, two seeds, every in-check target is given loss weight of 0.1, or 10% of in-check targets are kept at full weight. Both divide the summed loss by the number of eligible targets. The weighted minus the thinned logit competence at matched background loss, between 1.85 and 2.80 nats, is +0.009 logits (+0.002 and +0.016 in the two seeds). Delay curve and size term (Fig. B3). The pooled delay curve is least-squares fit of Δ𝐿 = 𝑏 (1 𝑓 𝑐) to the 50 thinned chess runs with an onset at 𝑞 = 0.75, across all sizes and both schedules, with 𝑏 = 0.77 0.07, 𝑐 = 0.28 0.03 and root-mean-square error of 0.020 nats. For the warm-upstabledecay runs, tokens to onset are read by linear interpolation between snapshots at the background loss of onset. The size term is the slope of the delay against log10 parameters at fixed fraction, pooled over fractions. On the constant learning rate it is 0.033 0.006, 0.014 0.007 and 0.002 0.007 nats per tenfold increase in size at 𝑞 = 0.70, 0.75 and 0.80, and on the warm-upstabledecay schedule 0.003 0.009 and 0.010 0.011 at 𝑞 = 0.75 and 0.80. At 𝑞 = 0.659, on the plateau of the fully supervised trajectories, it is 0.062 0.009 and 0.040 0.010 on the two schedules. Onsets are therefore read at 𝑞 0.70. B.4 Derived thinning relation Appendix gives the derivation. Errors of the derived offsets are taken over 1.852.80 nats at 9.7M and 1.852.05 nats at 64M. The sensitivity fitted to the pooled offsets at each background loss, across 2.2M431M and both schedules, is 0.550.67, with 𝜅 and 𝜏 fitted within shared window of background loss and 𝜅 resampled across runs. The slope of pooled logit competence against ln 𝑓 is 𝜅 𝑓 /( 𝑓 + 𝜏), so 𝜏 is the fraction at which the response to proportional thinning halves. Fitted across sizes with the pooled sensitivity, ln 𝜏 changes by +0.03 for each tenfold increase in parameters (95% interval 0.05 to +0.09) over 2.2M431M at fixed background loss. In the fit of the horizontal shift, 𝐴𝑘 (1 𝑓 𝑝), each of the 18 skills has its own amplitude 𝐴𝑘 and the exponent 𝑝 is shared; the fit is tested on another seed and on eight skills at 24M (Fig. B2cg). B.5 Held-out predictions The four chess tests hold out fractions below 0.1 (28 trajectories in 8 groups that share fully supervised trajectory), model sizes (99 in 12), the constant-learning-rate schedule (17 in 5) and the 1.28B and 3.0B models (2 in 2), and the error is pooled within each test. On web text, onsets are read against the held-out background loss outside all thinned targets, and the response is calibrated with censored fits of onset = 𝑔( 𝑓 ) + 𝑑 log10 (cid:19) (cid:18) 𝑁 𝑁 + 𝑒cell + 𝑒seed, 𝑔( 𝑓 ) = 𝑔1 + 𝑎 ln 𝑓 , (B1) where 𝑁 is the number of parameters, 𝑁 the geometric-mean size, 𝑑 the size term and 𝑒cell and 𝑒seed random effects. Nested closing is an evaluation subset of the closing mask. Neither 7B model is fully supervised on every skill, so each skill is compared across the two models, which differ in several thinned families at once; the isolated contrasts change one family at time. The error of 0.058 nats is the mean, over the six skills and the three seeds, of each seeds mean absolute difference between predicted and observed onset shift at competence levels 0.30.7 (0.055, 0.061 and 0.057 for the three seeds). The same two designs give 0.067 nats at 300M and 0.063 at 1B, with two seeds each. In the isolated contrasts every other family is fully supervised, and within seed the three runs share initialization, data order and mask hashes. Runs train to 2B tokens at 150M and 3B at 300M, and the agreement-thinned runs to 1B. The 150M offset, as function of background loss, is added to each 300M seeds fully supervised trajectory with 95% predictive band of 𝑡0.975,3 ˆ𝜎 1.25 from the four 150M seeds, and beyond the 150M range of background loss the offset at the edge is held. B.6 Document filtering In chess, 163M models were trained at 𝑓 = 1 and 0. The delay ratio at residual share is the delay of the filtered model divided by the delay of the model with in-check targets thinned to the same share, both read from the interval regression of onset on the loss before the first check at legal-move mass of 0.6. It is 0.87 at share of 0.1 (0.840.90 over sizes and seeds) and 0.78 at 0.03 (0.770.80). In SMILES, removing whole molecules brings ring closure 0.19 nats earlier than masking its targets when both are read on the shared background loss, and 0.05 nats later on each runs own training mixture (Fig. B4e). In web text, the Chinese label is the share of CJK characters, excluding kana and hangul. The classifiers have average precisions of 0.88, 0.98 and 0.98 for astronomy, Rust and Chinese, and at 𝑓 = 0 every reference-labelled document is removed as well. The Latin-square runs are accompanied by runs with thinned domain targets and with random residual (Fig. E2b). The realised share of the 7B Rust filter is 0.029. The background loss of the document-filtering runs leaves out the held-out targets in documents that resemble the three domains, about 2.6% of the targets. Onsets are read at half of each domains competence range. The effect of each filter on the other two domains is the onset fitted for domain at its own share and size minus the observed onset, plotted against the share kept by the other filter; the means lie within 0.03 nats of zero (Fig. E2e). sections.content: D.1 Acquisition cost after targets return Stored checkpoints hold the weights only, so the optimizer state is rebuilt at every return. Costs count the tokens after the targets return. The steps that rebuild the optimizer state contain none of the returned targets and are not charged; charging them gives 3.17.5% for the chess source runs at their lowest-loss checkpoints (Fig. D1e). With the warm-up at the return, no parameter update precedes the returned targets (Fig. D1b). Chess. Returns use the peak learning rate of the main recipe, 0.004. run stops after two consecutive evaluations with king-safety competence 𝑞 at or above 0.80 for 𝑠 = 1 and 0.70 for smaller shares, or at its token budget. Budgets grow as the returned share falls: 40M tokens at 𝑠 = 1, 60M at 0.3, 80M200M at 0.1 and 100M200M at 0.03; two returns at 𝑠 = 0.3 and 0.1 ran with the 40M budget. The 198 chess returns of the cost relation are the 110 returns with the warm-up before the return, the 82 returns with the warm-up at the return whose checkpoint and share have no return with the warm-up before it, and six returns of all targets from 9.7M and 64M checkpoints at 2.993.99 nats, which use the warm-up before the return and budget of 150M tokens. The two chess scores cross their levels together: at the first crossing of 𝑞 = 0.659 in return, the legal-move mass has median of 0.60, with 10th and 90th percentiles of 0.56 and 0.61 across 326 runs. Web text. The eleven source models are seed 0 at 9.7M, 24M, 64M and 163M, seeds 1 and 2 at 9.7M64M and seed 1 at 163M. After the moments are estimated the first moment is set to zero, and the 30 steps on the source models own targets run at the learning rate of the source schedule, 0.008. Targets return from 79 checkpoints of each source run. Evaluations fall at steps 06, 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16 and then at steps 15% apart. run stops once competence is at 0.90, or at twice the steps of its first evaluation at or above 0.85 with at least 24 steps, or at its budget, which is 60M tokens for returns near or above the acquisition loss and 30M otherwise; every run reached the level. SMILES. Returns continue the data order of the source run at learning rate of 0.004. Evaluations fall when the targets return and then at steps spaced by factor of 1.25. run stops after two consecutive evaluations at 0.75 or above (0.7 at shares below 1) or at budget of 20M, 30M, 60M and 100M tokens for shares of 1, 0.3, 0.1 and 0.03. Othello. The eight source runs are four at 9.7M (two seeds trained with none of the forced-pass targets, and one each with 10% and 30%), two at 24M (none and 10%) and two at 64M (10% and 30%), and their checkpoints lie at background losses of 2.122.86 nats. Returns use learning rate of 0.004, with the moments estimated over 20 steps without parameter updates, and are evaluated on the chess schedule. run stops after two consecutive evaluations at 0.6 or above. Eleven runs were at the level when the targets returned and are counted as one step, and three more reached it within the first step; these fourteen are upper bounds. D.2 Logit distance and the cost relation The reference has seed other than that of the source run for 50 chess, 21 web-text and 2 Othello runs. References cover 186 of 198 chess runs, 88 of 90 web-text runs, 66 of 73 SMILES runs and 50 of 53 Othello runs. For the progress term and the split at 𝐿(𝑠), the acquisition loss is read from one curve per domain, fitted across sizes and returned shares in chess, across returned shares at 9.7M in SMILES and across sizes in web text; it lies within 0.04 nats of the value from the same-size reference in chess and SMILES and within 0.08 nats in web text. Table D1 gives the fits. In SMILES the rate is 0.74 0.21, 0.57 0.10, 0.47 0.08 and 0.52 0.09 decades per logit at 9.7M, 24M, 64M and 163M. The 13 returns of all ring-closure targets from logit distance below 1.3 reached the level within 1420 steps, inside the 20-step warm-up, at every size; without the returns of 25 steps or fewer the rate is 0.56 0.18. For the 56 runs returned above the acquisition loss with positive logit distance that reached the level in chess, web text and SMILES, the background loss at which they reached the 36 acquisition level differed from 𝐿 (𝑠) by median of 0.04 nats in chess and web text and 0.01 nats in SMILES (Fig. D2h), and the two-part form with the single line gave their costs with median absolute error of 0.17 dex. Across seven acquisition levels in chess the rate is 0.781.20 decades per logit (Fig. D2b). The standard errors of the single line and of the trend with model size are clustered by source run. One never-supervised Othello return, from checkpoint 1.5 logits above the acquisition loss, did not reach the level within 306 steps. In the near-floor ordering higher score counts as lower predicted cost. D.3 Batch size and learning rate at the return The three checkpoints of each size are the first stored checkpoint at or below the acquisition loss, the lowest-loss checkpoint and the one nearest the midpoint of the two in background loss. Every setting is evaluated at every step up to step 40. The runs from initialization have two seeds at 9.7M and 24M and one at 64M. Table D2 gives every cost. Training from initialization needed 0.550.66 times the tokens at 16 sequences and 2.23.3 times at 256. At the standard learning rate, the five returns of 25216 optimizer steps needed 1.11.65 times the tokens at 16 sequences, in 4.36.6 times as many steps, and 1.52.2 times the tokens at 256 sequences. With 16 sequences at one third of the learning rate, the tokens were 0.711.07 times those of the standard setting at 2.84.3 times the steps. Returns that finish within ten optimizer steps needed fewer tokens at 16 sequences, 0.420.94 times, so the costs of 0.100.78% from the lowest-loss checkpoints are upper estimates of the data required. From the lowest-loss checkpoints the cost was 0.151.35% of the tokens from initialization at the same setting across the five settings. The slope of log10 relative cost against the logit distance of the checkpoint was 0.861.29 decades per logit at the four other settings, and the single line of Fig. 4b gave the relative costs at the five settings with mean errors of 0.40 to 0.12 dex. From initialization the permuted rule needed 1.031.13 times the tokens of the true rule at these settings. D.4 Transplanted weight changes Table D3 gives the legal-move mass and the change in background loss for every change and recipient checkpoint. At 9.7M the Frobenius norm of the change due to the returned targets was 1.7% of that of the final weights for the 619M-token checkpoint and 11% for the 97M-token checkpoint; at 64M, relative to the weights of its own checkpoint, it was 0.80.9% at 1.93B tokens, 1.5% at 226M and 3.23.3% at 161M. Legal-move mass and background loss were evaluated on the 1,000 held-out games used for the returns. At 9.7M, across the checkpoints with measured acquisition cost, nine in one seed and six in the other, the rank correlation between the recipients cost and the mass gained was 0.85 and 0.49 for the change from the 193M-token checkpoint. The weight change of return without the subtraction of its control run raised legal-move mass at other checkpoints similarly but raised background loss by 0.160.26 nats for the changes from 619M, 290M and 193M tokens and by 0.320.44 for the change from 97M, as did the change of the control run alone; the cosine similarity between the two was 0.860.98. Changes computed at different checkpoints of run had cosine similarity of 0.060.23 with one another and of 0.00 between seeds. At 64M the Gaussian change gained between 0.010 and 0.001 and the change added to the other seeds checkpoints between 0.000 and +0.002 in legal-move mass. No 163M model was trained from initialization on the schedule of the return runs, so the two 163M cases are divided by the tokens at which the fully supervised 163M training run of the same seed reaches the level (142.8M). Web text. The agreement targets are the six number-marked auxiliaries, and competence is the preference for the auxiliary over its number partner. For each of two seeds, one fully supervised model and one model without agreement targets are trained from initialization for 1.07B tokens; the cases are steps 1,448 and 4,096 of each seed, at background losses of 4.144.19 and 3.653.67 nats. The withdrawn route continues the fully supervised model from an earlier step without agreement targets until it has read the rows of the never-supervised model at the case step (111M or 315M tokens). Gradient ascent keeps the state of lowest competence whose background loss is at most 0.05 nats above the start. Ascent on the full cross-entropy at the agreement targets lowers the probability of every auxiliary and changes the choice between them little, whereas the two-way loss acts on the choice that competence scores (open and filled diamonds in Fig. F1ik). Five unlearned models were at the acquisition level when the targets returned. At the return the background losses of the routes of case lie within 0.04 nats. The removed models reach the level within one to three optimizer steps, so each ratio is resolved to about factor of 1.5. With 10% returned they reached it in 7 of 8 cases within the budget of 8M tokens, and all 24 other models reached it at 0.271.4%. The variance between and within source runs of the reference is taken to be the same for the compared models, and the interval uses 𝑡 quantiles on the references degrees of freedom. 46 F.3 Related king-safety positions Inputs stay intact in every family-masking run, and background loss is measured on targets outside check and outside the masked families. Adapters 𝑊 𝑥 + 𝐵𝐴𝑥 are placed on all seven linear maps of every block, with 𝐴 uniform in 𝑑 1/2 and 𝐵 = 0 at the start, and all other weights are held fixed. Trainable groups keep their learning rates, and adapters take the rate of the hidden matrices without weight decay. Where no multiplier gave permuted return that reached the level, the multiplier with the highest final permuted mass was used; the unrestricted return uses the standard learning rate. The first block alone cost 3950 times at 64M and did not reach the level at 9.7M and 24M, and the unembedding with the final norm cost 1213 times at 64M and did not reach it at 9.7M and 24M. Adapters of rank 1, 4 and 16 cost 3.358, 2.27.4 and 1.33.1 times. Both rules reached 0.6 under 19 restrictions, only the true rule under 36 and neither under 9. The best multiplier lay at the top of the grid for rank-1 adapters, for rank-4 adapters at 64M and for the rank-16 adapter of one 64M run, so the adapter costs are upper estimates. Stitched models. sections.title: G Statistics
sections.content: In the analyses of acquisition cost point is one return run, and source run is one training run at one seed, shared by its checkpoints. Least-squares rates for single domains are given with the larger of the ordinary and the cluster-robust standard error. Along thinned trajectory, the offsets at interpolated background losses are repeated measurements of that trajectory, so errors of the derived relation are taken over models and held-out prediction errors are given per trajectory. Probabilities of output classes have intervals from 1,000 bootstrap resamples of games, and the isolated web-text contrasts have 𝑡 intervals over four seeds. The family-masking contrast has two paired seeds, so the range over the 16 recombinations of seeds is shown in place of sampling interval.
